notes: **Item R1 of the Results voice review: Ch. 1** (Characterization of wild barley grain nutritional value traits). This is S. Hübner's text from the mini paper, kept wherever it holds. The item fixes the three things from my review list (the chapter no longer followed the new Fig. 1; an interpretation sentence; unclear sentences) and one factual slip.

**¶1 (small fixes):** "roughly twice that of all other traits" was wrong for flowering time (H² 0.747 > 0.474), so it now says **the other nutritional traits**. "Indicating the respective genetic control for these traits" is removed as too vague. The last sentence ("Overall, results were consistent with the heritability with substantial variation …") is reworded with the same claim.

**¶2 → two paragraphs, in the order of the new Fig. 1:**
> - **¶2 = trait correlations (Fig. 1c).** The r values for the morphological traits are now given; before, the text said only "strongly". Grain number is added (starch −0.25, fiber +0.39), because the Discussion's "higher grain numbers" argument rests on it. "β-glucan and protein displayed weaker, mostly negative correlations" is replaced by what the figure shows: β-glucan–flowering time is −0.37, as strong as starch–flowering time.
> - **¶3 = environment (Fig. 1d)**, opened with Sariel's own aim sentence ("To examine whether variation … followed the environmental gradient …"). The site plot, now an Online Resource, moves from the opening to the end, as supporting evidence, with Sariel's wording.

**Removed as interpretation** (major item 3), because the Discussion says both: "linking grain composition directly to whole-plant resource allocation and phenology" (Discussion §2 ¶1) and "Together, these associations linked … soil texture and precipitation…" (Discussion §1).
**Unchanged:** the heritability and G×E numbers, all environmental correlations, Sariel's opening sentence with its method clause, and the Fig. 1 caption.

**Applied 2026-10-01 with the user's decisions:** Q1 keep S. Hübner's 'Together …' sentence (now the closing sentence, after the site-plot sentence); ¶1 'indicating the respective genetic control…' kept; ¶2 correlation sentences unchanged (the r-value additions and the β-glucan/protein rewrite dropped); split, environment opener and site-plot sentence applied.

edits.old: To examine whether variation in grain nutritional traits followed the environmental gradient of the collection sites, trait BLUPs were first visualized across the 29 sites ordered by ecological region ([TODO: ESM number, fixed when the Online Resources are numbered (supplementary/supplementary.md): the site figure, former Fig. 2a (centered trait BLUPs of the four nutritional traits across the 29 sampling sites, ordered and colored by ecological region), moved to the Online Resources on S. Hübner's comment (2026-09-30). PDF: 08_USED_creating_figures/Figure_ESM_site_BLUPs/ESM_site_BLUPs.pdf (make_figure_ESM_site_BLUPs.R); caption draft in supplementary/supplementary.md. Also cited in the Discussion (TODOs 421, 422). Could be merged with the sampling-site Online Resource (TODO 218)]{.comment-start id="321" author="TODO"}[[Online Resource N]]{.mark}[]{.comment-end id="321"}). This descriptive pattern suggested that northern-derived genotypes generally had higher starch, whereas desert-derived genotypes tended to have lower starch and higher fiber and β-glucan; protein showed no clear directional trend. Among the nutritional traits, starch was strongly negatively correlated with fiber (r = −0.78; Fig. 1c) and β-glucan (r = −0.53), while fiber and β-glucan were positively correlated (r = 0.35; all *P* \< 0.001). Thus, genotypes with higher starch tended to have lower fiber and β-glucan. Protein was poorly correlated with other traits, and significant negative correlation was obtained only for protein-starch (r = −0.12, *P* \< 0.05). Among the morphological and phenological traits, starch was strongly correlated with grain weight, plant height, and flowering time, while fiber showed the exact opposite pattern. Protein was also weakly negatively correlated with grain weight (r = −0.13, *P* \< 0.05). Overall, β-glucan and protein displayed weaker, mostly negative correlations, linking grain composition directly to whole-plant resource allocation and phenology (Fig. 1c). To identify which environmental variables of the sites of origin were associated with each trait, site-mean nutritional-trait BLUPs were correlated with eight environmental variables (Fig. 1d). Starch was positively correlated with clay, precipitation, and organic carbon, and negatively correlated with sand and pH. Fiber showed the opposite pattern for clay, sand, and precipitation, while β-glucan was positively correlated with sand and electrical conductivity and negatively correlated with clay, precipitation, and organic carbon. Protein was not significantly correlated with any of the measured environmental variables. Together, these associations linked the contrasting patterns of starch versus fiber and β-glucan to gradients in soil texture and precipitation, consistent with the broader geographic pattern observed across the collection sites.
